text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least five people were killed in clashes near the mid-western oil city of Warri.
- Nigeria's external reserves rose to 78.56 billion naira at the end of November from 59.79 billion naira a month earlier.
- Chairman of "Vision 2010" economic think-tank, Ernest Shonekan, says France can play a major role in helping to secure debt relief for Nigeria and should also increase business ties.
- Police have detained about 620 suspects in connection with ethnic violence around Warri.

- A government minister says that groups campaigning for military ruler General Sani Abacha to stay in office after a 1998 handover to civilian rule are within their rights. Another minister earlier this month said the proliferation of such groups would tarnish the image of the plan to restore democracy.

- The government's decision to remove textiles from the list of prohibited imports may provide opportunities for exports from Korea. A mission to Nigeria from the Korean textile industry will arrive in May.
- Foreign shipping companies may divert their goods to neighbouring countries if government imposes new rules on shipping charges.
- Nigerian Railways Corporation restarts freight transport after a four-year break.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation awaits orders from the oil ministry on resuming insurance contacts with the National Insurance Company Of Nigeria.
